root.name: Modern Defense: Masur Gambit
root.moves: 1. e4 g6 2. d4 Nh6 3. Nc3 f5 4. Bxh6 Bxh6 5. exf5 O-O

overview: Black plays ...Nh6 and ...f5 against 2.d4, and after Bxh6 Bxh6 exf5 O-O gives a pawn for quick development and the h6 bishop eyeing d2/c1. White has the extra pawn and the choice of d5 or Nf3/Qd2 to blunt the bishop. Black's compensation is thin and strong players do not rate the gambit.

white_ideas.idea: Keep the extra pawn with Qd2 or Nge2 and neutralise the h6 bishop
Develop calmly and return the pawn only if needed

black_ideas.idea: Use the lead in development and the open f-file for pressure
Trade the dark bishops and hit the d4 centre with ...d5 or ...Nc6

typical_structures.structure: White up a pawn with a healthy e-pawn gone from the centre; Black has open f-file and bishop on h6

character.notes: Black needs to create threats to justify the pawn.

gambit.notes: Black gives the f-pawn; White can keep it.

sublines_that_differ.name: Declined
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 g6 2. d4 Nh6 3. Nc3 f5 4. Bxh6
sublines_that_differ.how: If White avoids exf5 the gambit is not accepted

character.reason: A gambit with early forcing play and risks for Black.

gambit.reason: Black gives the f-pawn for development.

soundness.reason: The pawn is not fully compensated.

structure.reason: e-pawns gone, open f-file for Black.

approach.reason: Strong players seldom choose this gambit.

level.reason: Dubious, so not beginner; little theory.
